text:
Maya: Heads-up — planning a staggered cohort drain in us-east1 tonight 00:30–03:30 UTC. Targeting ~10% of GPU pools for an NVLink microcode bump.
Liam: ETA on capacity impact?
Maya: Expect transient preempts, roughly 7–12% reduction in burstable GPU capacity while each cohort drains (~45m per cohort). We'll sequence cohorts to keep application p99 latency impact <2%.
Jordan: Which cohorts/pools are you touching? can you list racks?
Maya: Cohort order: cohort-A (racks 7,8), cohort-B (racks 9,10), cohort-C (racks 11,12). Pools: gpu-highmem-01..03 and gpu-standard-05..06.
Anika: @Maya please add a KV cache seeding step after each reboot — last time we saw cold-cache tail latency and token cost spike.
Maya: Will do. Preflight checklist (quick):
```
- confirm cohort membership and owners
- cordon + drain cohort-A
- run kvseed with parallelism 4
- watch p99 and token cost dashboards
- uncordon after health checks pass
- if p99 > 15% sustained for 5m -> abort and roll back
```
Priya: Ops-bot, can you create a short incident page if we exceed thresholds?
ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance created for cohort drain in us-east1 @ 2026-03-22T00:30Z. Owners: Maya, Liam, Jordan, Anika. Automated alerts enabled.
Liam: Cost note — are we spinning up extra capacity (spots/dedicated) for the window? that will drive short-term billing.
Maya: We have 30 spare reserved GPUs in us-east1 across Dedicated pools; plan is to enable them first (no incremental cloud spend). Cross-region fallback (eu-west1) is last resort and would add estimated egress + runtime ~$120/hr if used.
Jordan: Cross-region introduces networking/egress risk. Prefer intra-region failover.
Anika: Agreed. We'll try to avoid cross-region unless absolutely necessary. If we do route, we'll limit to non-Latin locale workloads to minimize user impact.
Maya: Canary strategy: enable canary on cohort-A after drain, run synthetic load for 10m, check token cost and p99. Canary IDs: canary-us-east-cohortA-01. I'll post results at T-2h and again at T-15m.
Liam: I'll be on watch 00:15–04:00 UTC. If I see sustained p99 > 15% for >5m I'll hit abort.
Priya: I'll prep priority-tenant comms in case latency increases. Draft message ready to send if canary fails.
Anika: Runbook KV seed command to include in notes:
```
./kvseed --pool gpu-highmem-01 --parallel 6 --warm-prefixes 1000 --timeout 20m
```
Maya: Also applying a temporary per-request batch cap for hosted API routes during the window (cap=4) to smooth latency while pools are reduced.
Jordan: Can we shorten cache TTL to 30s during roll to reduce staleness and encourage faster cache warm-ups?
Maya: Yes, patching the TTL now in control plane.
Liam: If we see a P95 degradation > 10% but P99 stable, proceed but continue close monitoring.
Maya: ops-bot will auto-post to #incidents if p99 > 15% sustained. I'll update the maintenance PR with exact cohort member IDs and the post-drain health checks.
Priya: Thanks — waiting on canary IDs. :thumbsup:
Maya: Posting canary IDs and a short timeline at T-2h. Owners: @Liam (oncall), @Jordan (sre), @Anika (infra), @Priya (cs) :eyes:
Liam: ack.
